If he found it in the place, etc. And Taz wrote that if he returned and found it, even though he did not pay attention whether it is in the place where he left it or not — they are not accustomed to forbid it, even in a place where most slaughterers are idolaters, etc., end of his words. And it requires further study from where he derived this; for from the Rosh's words, who wrote the reason that we are not concerned for a raven that exchanged it and brought it to that very place — it implies: but otherwise it is forbidden; and so is the implication of the poskim who wrote that ravens from their locale take:
In a place where all the sellers are Israelites who sell kosher meat. Meaning: it is known that they never sell except kosher meat; if not so — such as when they sometimes sell treifah meat, in a place where they announce that there is treifah and they announced — then even because of one treifah they forbid all the pieces; and when meat is found there it is forbidden because it has the status of kavu'a. And likewise if meat is found in the hand of an idolater — forbidden; and even though most animals are presumed kosher — nevertheless it is a rabbinic enactment not to buy from the idolater l'chatchila in a place where they do not announce, or in a place where they announce and announced thus — so wrote Tosafot Chullin (daf 95a) in the section 'and regarding found,' etc. — see there:
That all the sellers, etc. 'All' is not precise — the majority is like the whole. (Payment of these laws is in siman 1 seif 4 and siman 110 and 118 and what is written there):
And there are those who permit. Thus wrote the Ran in the name of Sefer HaTerumah: presumably it is permitted only regarding meat found in a city whose slaughterers are Israelites, for we are not concerned for ravens of the world; or alternatively, in a city whose slaughterers are idolaters — such as when he left it in his house and found it in the place where he left it — for in every such case we are not concerned for a raven; but in a city whose slaughterers are idolaters, and he found it in a place where he did not leave it — we are concerned, lest ravens from their locale took it, and these idolaters require siman or teviyat ayin and did not find it in the place where he left it, end of his words. And he means: a city where most slaughterers are idolaters — and so wrote Rashba in his novellae in the name of Sefer HaTerumah, and ruled thus. And it is explained in Rashba that the same applies if pieces of meat are found on the road — and likewise if most passersby on the road are Israelites — permitted, and we are not concerned for a raven as long as we do not see that a raven took it; and all the more so if he found meat in the market in a place where most slaughterers are Israelites — permitted. All this is the view of the aforementioned poskim (and so wrote Rokeach siman 97, that one who finds an animal and the like in a place where most are Israelites — permitted, and we are not concerned for meat that disappeared from sight; and so Issur VeHeter general rule 22 din 7: where he left meat in the street in a place where most idolaters are found, and he went and returned and found it in the place where he left it — permitted, end of his words). And it appears that such is also the Rosh's view in the name of Rashbam in all this — for behold he comes to settle why Rashba ruled like the plain meaning of the mishnah, that it deals with meat found in the market where most are Israelites; and further that he wrote (to settle that incident in Perek Elu Metziot that deals with a majority of Israelites). But where ravens took and returned it — we are concerned perhaps they exchanged; it implies: presumably when we did not see that it was taken we are not concerned in a majority of Israelites. And further that he wrote that these incidents in the Gemara that required simanim or teviyat ayin — one may say they were in a city that is mostly idolaters; and since it was lost there is greater concern — and these incidents imply that he did not find it in the place where he left it, as the aforementioned poskim wrote. And also from the Rosh's words, who wrote 'and since it was lost,' etc. — it implies thus; and so Bach, that the Rosh holds those incidents were where he did not find it in the place where he left it — and nevertheless they forbade only in a majority of idolaters. And further, presumably that which the Rosh wrote 'and since it was lost there is greater concern' comes to say that it was lost and he found it not in the place where he left it — for otherwise why say it at all; and 'and since it was lost,' etc. — it should have said only that it deals with a majority of idolaters; rather, certainly he holds that in a majority of idolaters alone they did not forbid except where there is also the circumstance that it was lost. And what the Rosh wrote at the beginning of his words, that that which we are not concerned for meat that disappeared from sight is where he found the meat in the place where he left it — that we are not concerned perhaps ravens exchanged it and brought it to that very place — he means: we are not concerned at all for meat that disappeared from sight, even in a majority of idolaters. All this is clear according to the Rosh and Rashbam; and so is proven explicitly in Asheri Perek Elu Metziot — see there; and so in Darkei Moshe, that the Rosh's view is like Sefer HaTerumah; and so is implied in Maharshal Chullin siman 22; and so in Derishah and Perishah in this siman and siman 1 — not like Bach in this siman seif 4, who went outside the line of reasoning and did not understand the Rosh's words thus; and therefore he entered great forced explanations and challenged Derishah and Perishah in the last section improperly. And the matters are clear as I wrote. Also that which Bach wrote that such is the Tur's and Rabbenu Yerucham's view like his words — it is not so — see there. (And he explained that incident of Rav Kahana where ravens threw kidneys, etc., and they found it in the place where he left it — and this is a matter that has no dawn; and in Perek Elu Metziot the Rosh explained explicitly like Tosafot Chullin, that incident of Rav Kahana was in all places around which most were Israelites — see there. He also forced to explain that Rashbam did not need to say according to his view that those incidents were mostly idolaters, etc. — all these are forced and far-fetched.) The Tur wrote in the name of Rashba that even if he left ten and found nine — they are forbidden, for we are concerned perhaps those were taken and these are others; and in Taharat HaKodesh they learned from chametz. And the Rambam wrote in Taharat HaKodesh at the end of general rule 32 that the custom is not like Rashba when he left ten and found nine, but rather they permit in every case; and so Issur VeHeter general rule 22 din 10 wrote that it is permitted when he left ten and found nine, for we say a cat or mouse dragged it; and even a complete half-rib, lest a mouse stole it, end of his words. However, one may say that the Rav in Taharat HaKodesh did not say that they are accustomed to be lenient except regarding pieces that are not tied — for such is the custom to leave several pieces together without being tied; and in such a case perhaps he holds like Tosafot's and the Tur's view in Orach Chaim siman 439, that regarding chametz too it is forbidden only when tied together; and the Mechaber brought it in Orach Chaim there. But when tied one may not be lenient, since in such a case regarding chametz all forbid; and Rashba and Ra'ah daf 122 forbade here where there is no majority of permissibility; and so Taz wrote anonymously that when he left ten and found nine it is forbidden; and so Maharshal Chullin siman 22, that when tied it is obviously forbidden, but when not tied it appears to him to permit, since the Rambam testified that such is the custom; and Issur VeHeter permits entirely; and so Maharshal there permits when not tied. And it is possible that Rashba and Ra'ah themselves forbade only when tied, like Tosafot's view regarding chametz; and so Perishah in the name of his teacher, that Rashba deals with such a case — not like Bach in the last section seif 5, who challenged Derishah and wrote: 'And in my composition I brought that Rashba himself wrote that here even when not tied,' etc. — and he erred in his own words, for in his composition he wrote thus from his own words after Rashba's words, and understood that it is the conclusion of Rashba's words; and it is not so, for it is not found at all in Rashba's words — see there:

ויש מתירין כו'. היינו כלוי דפליג על רב בטור הביא דעת הרשב"א שסובר אפילו הניח י' ומצא ט' אסור דחיישינן שמא ניטלו ואלו אחרים הם וא"ל מ"ש מחמץ בפסח בא"ח סי' תל"ט בסעיף ג' די"א ה"מ בקשורים יחד דוקא הכא שאני שכיון שראו חכמים לגזור בבשר שנתעלם מן העין גזרו בכ"מ שאנו רואין שנעשה בבשר זה שום שינוי בעולם חיישינן אח"כ לכל מה דאפשר לחוש דעשו חיזוק לדבריהם כנ"ל:
והמנהג להקל כו'. היינו בזמן שמוצאו במקום שהניחו אבל מצאו במקום אחר אפילו אם הוא בביתו אסור אם אין לו בו סימן או טביעות עין. כ' המרדכי פ' ג"ה וז"ל מעשה בא לידי בתרנגולת שחוט' ושלחוה ביד עובד כוכבים בלא שומר ונסתפקו לומר שמא אחרת היתה ונתחלפה והלכו לשוחט ושאלו לו אם שחט זאת התרנגולת ואמר אין לי בה טביעות עין אמנם עתה שחטתי תרנגולת אחת אבל בעל התרנגולת היה מכיר אותה ואמר שזאת היא והתרתי אותה כיון שבעל התרנגולת מכירה כר"ת דאמר לית הלכתא כרב דאמר בשר שנתעלם מן העין אסור כו' עכ"ל והקשה ב"י דהא רב נמי מכשיר ביש טביעות עין דט"ע עדיף מסימן כדאיתא בגמרא עכ"ל וכתב עליו רש"ל חוץ מכבודו לא הבין כי לרב לא מהני ט"ע דתרנגולת דשמא לא שחטה הישראל אלא עובד כוכבים שחטה דהא שחיטה לאו סימן וא"כ לרב דחייש לשמא החליפו ה"נ דחיישינן לכה"ג אבל מאחר דקי"ל כלוי דס"ל לא חיישינן שמא הוחלפו ה"נ לא חיישינן לכה"ג מאחר דלא חזינן ריעותא ואמרינן בודאי היא התרנגולת ששחטה ישראל מאחר שהוא אומר עתה שחטתי תרנגולת א' עכ"ל משמע שפירש דברי המרדכי ששלחו הישראל לעובד כוכבים עם התרנגולת שיוליכנה לישראל לשחוט ואמר שמא העובד כוכבים שחטה לזאת ואין פירושו נראה כלל דהרי המרדכי כ' בתרנגולת שחוטה ושלחוה ביד עובד כוכבים כו' משמע דכבר היתה שחוטה ותו דלמה אמר שנסתפקו אם נחלפה למה להם חשש החילוף היה להם לחוש שמא זאת היא אלא שהעובד כוכבים שחטה ותו למה כתב דללוי כשר דודאי לוי מודה דחיישינן שמא העובד כוכבים שחטה כל שלא נתברר שישראל שחטה אם העובד כוכבים מביא תרנגולת ישראל שחוטה אע"פ שידוע לנו שישראל שחט אחת מ"מ מאן יימר דזו היא דהא אין כאן רוב טבחי ישראל וע"כ לומר דהשוחט אומר בפירוש ששחט אחת לעובד כוכבים זה וכיון שהבעל מכירה לזאת ודאי היא דודאי לא נימא דהעובד כוכבי' נתן אחרת לישראל לשחוט ולזו שחט בעצמו להכשיל לישראל הא לא חיישינן דהלכתא רווחת בסי' קי"ח דלא חיישינן לחליפות עובד כוכבים אלא במקום שיש לו הנאה ממנה וזה מותר אפי' לרב דכ"ע ס"ל לההוא דסימן קי"ח אפי' הרי"ף והרמב"ם והש"ע שפסקו כאן כרב וא"כ הדרא קושיא לדוכתא על המרדכי ותו דהא המרדכי לא כתב שהשוחט אומר עתה לעובד כוכבים זה ומו"ח ז"ל הלך ג"כ בעקבי רש"ל בפירוש דברי המרדכי ופי' שאסור לרב לפי שא"א להכירה בטביעות עין שהרי כשהוליכה לשחוט היתה חיה ועכשיו היא שחוטה כו' וגם על זה קשה דא"כ ללוי נמי ניחוש בהא מחמת חשש שחיטה ותו דהא אמרי' בהדיא בגמ' פ' אלו מציאות בכמה אמוראי שמצאו עופות שלהם שחוטים ברוב טבחי ישראל וכן בברייתא הרי שנגנבו גדייו ומצאן שחוטין כו' ומשמע דמהני בהם טביעות עין וזה פשוט וא"כ יפה תמה מאור עינינו הב"י ויפה הבין אלא שנלע"ד לתרץ דברי המרדכי בענין זה דודאי מיירי כפשוטן של דברים שכבר נשחטה התרנגולת זאת בהיתר אלא שאחד שלח לחבירו התרנגולת השחוט' ע"י עובד כוכבים בלא שומר והמרדכי ס"ל דלא מהני סימן או טביעות עין לרב אלא במקום שאין ריעותא וסברא לחילוף אלא מצד חומרא בעלמא כגון שנמצא איזה בשר ביד עובד כוכבים שלקח לעצמו ורוב המוכרים ישראל למה לנו לומר שהחליפה אלא חומרא החמירו בזה שצריך סימן לדעת הרמב"ם שפוסק כותי' בסעיף א' אבל אם ישראל שולח ביד עובד כוכבים בשר או עוף שחוט שיש חשש שהעובד כוכבים החליף להנאתו שהניח אחרת גרועה הימנה בזה נחית דרגא לרב דלא מהני סימן כל דהו או ט"ע דשמא העובד כוכבים זייף ועשה ג"כ סימן זה כגון ההיא סימן שסמך עליה רב שחתך הבשר בתלת קרנתא ודאי אם רוצה העובד כוכבים לזייף להנאתו יטריח עצמו גם בזה דמה אומנות יש בחתוך זה וכן טביעות עין לא מהני דשמא טרח עצמו והביא אחרת שדומה לזו במראה דזה הוא דבר מצוי אבל [לוי] לא חש כ"כ ולדידיה גם בשולח ע"י עובד כוכבים סגי בטביעות עין וכן משמע מדברי המרדכי שכתב קודם למעשה זה ופר"ת דלית הלכתא כרב כו' הלכך אם הניח חתיכת בשר כו' אבל אם מצאה במקום אחר חיישינן עד שיהיה לו בה סימנים ויכירנה בטביעות עין (פי' או יכירנה) וכן אם שלחה ביד עובד כוכבים הדין כן דהא אמרינן בפרק אין מעמידין (עבודה זרה דף ל"ט) חבי"ת אסורים בחותם א' עכ"ל דלכאורה קשה למה כתב האי וכן כו' ומה חידש בו כאן ולפי מ"ש ניחא דלרב לא הוי מותר כאן בטביעות עין וכיון דקי"ל כלוי מותר בטביעות עין. וא"כ יפה כתב המרדכי כאן בשולח תרנגולת שחוטה ע"י עובד כוכבים דתחלה רצו לבקש היתר מחמת השוחט אם יכירנה ולא עלתה בידם והתירו מחמת הכרת בעל התרנגולת בטביעות עין והיינו כלוי כמ"ש כנ"ל:

And there are those who permit, etc. This is Levi, who argues with Rav; the Tur brought Rashba's view, who holds that even if he left ten and found nine — forbidden, for we are concerned perhaps those were taken and these are others. And one may ask: what is different from chametz on Pesach in Orach Chaim siman 439 seif 3, where some say this applies only when tied together? Here it is different, for since the Sages saw fit to decree on meat that disappeared from sight, they decreed in every place where we see that some change occurred to this meat in the world — we are concerned afterward for everything one might fear; they strengthened their words, as explained above:
And the custom is to be lenient, etc. This is when he finds it in the place where he left it; but if he found it elsewhere, even in his house — forbidden if he has no siman or teviyat ayin. Mordechai wrote in Perek Gittin, and thus: an incident came before me with a slaughtered chicken that they sent in the hand of an idolater without a guard, and they were in doubt to say perhaps it was another and was exchanged; and they went to the slaughterer and asked him if he slaughtered this chicken, and he said: I have no teviyat ayin upon it; however, I have just now slaughtered one chicken; but the chicken's owner recognized it and said this is it, and I permitted it, since the owner recognizes it like Rabbenu Tam, who said the halacha is not like Rav who said meat that disappeared from sight is forbidden, etc., end of his words. And Beit Yosef challenged: behold Rav too permits when there is teviyat ayin, for teviyat ayin is preferable to siman, as stated in the Gemara, end of his words. And Rashal wrote on this: besides his honor he did not understand, for according to Rav teviyat ayin does not help regarding a chicken, lest the Israelite did not slaughter it but an idolater slaughtered it — for shechitah is not a siman; if so, according to Rav who is concerned lest they exchanged it — here too we are concerned for such a case. But since it is settled like Levi, who holds we are not concerned lest they were exchanged — here too we are not concerned for such a case, since we do not see a suspicious circumstance, and we say: certainly it is the chicken that the Israelite slaughtered, since he says: I have just now slaughtered one chicken, end of his words — it implies he explained Mordechai's words that they sent the Israelite with the chicken via an idolater to bring it to an Israelite to slaughter, and he said perhaps the idolater slaughtered this one; and his explanation does not appear at all, for behold Mordechai wrote regarding a slaughtered chicken that they sent in the hand of an idolater, etc. — it implies it was already slaughtered. And further, why did he say they were in doubt if it was exchanged — they should have had concern perhaps this is it; rather that the idolater slaughtered it. And further, why did he write that for Levi it is kosher — certainly Levi agrees we are concerned lest the idolater slaughtered it, as long as it is not clarified that an Israelite slaughtered it; if an idolater brings a slaughtered chicken of an Israelite, even though we know an Israelite slaughtered one — nevertheless who will say this is it, for there is no majority of Israelite slaughterers here; and therefore one must say that the slaughterer explicitly says he slaughtered one for this idolater, and since the owner recognizes this one with certainty — certainly we do not say the idolater gave another to an Israelite to slaughter and slaughtered this one himself to trap the Israelite; we are not concerned, for the halacha is widespread in siman 118 that we are not concerned for exchanges by idolaters except where he has benefit from it — and this is permitted even according to Rav, for all hold like that law in siman 118, even Rif and Rambam and Shulchan Aruch who ruled here like Rav; if so, the challenge returns to its place against Mordechai. And further, Mordechai did not write that the slaughterer says 'now' to this idolater — and Maharshal also followed Rashal in explaining Mordechai's words, and explained that it is forbidden according to Rav because one cannot recognize it by teviyat ayin, for when he brought it to slaughter it was alive and now it is slaughtered, etc. And this too is difficult, for then according to Levi we should also be concerned because of concern for shechitah. And further, we say explicitly in the Gemara Perek Elu Metziot with several amoraim that they found their birds slaughtered among a majority of Israelite slaughterers; and likewise in a baraita: his kids were stolen and he found them slaughtered, etc. — and it implies teviyat ayin helps for them; and this is simple. If so, Beit Yosef wondered well and understood well; only it appears to me to answer Mordechai's words on this matter: certainly it deals according to the plain meaning of the matter, that this chicken was already slaughtered permissibly; only that one sent his fellow the slaughtered chicken via an idolater without a guard, and Mordechai holds that for Rav siman or teviyat ayin does not help except where there is no suspicious circumstance and reason for exchange, but from mere general stringency — such as when some meat is found in the hand of an idolater who took for himself and most sellers are Israelites — why should we say it was exchanged; they were stringent in this that a siman is needed, according to Rambam who rules like him in seif 1. But if an Israelite sends via an idolater slaughtered meat or a bird where there is concern the idolater exchanged for his benefit, leaving another worse than it — here we descend a level according to Rav, that neither any siman nor teviyat ayin helps, lest the idolater forged and also made this siman, such as that siman Rav relied on, that he cut the meat in three corners — certainly if the idolater wants to forge for his benefit he will trouble himself also in this; what craftsmanship is there in this cut. And likewise teviyat ayin does not help, lest he troubled himself and brought another that resembles this one in appearance — this is common. But Levi was not so concerned, and according to him even when sending via an idolater teviyat ayin suffices; and so is implied from Mordechai's words who wrote before this incident, and Rabbenu Tam: the halacha is not like Rav, etc.; therefore if he left a piece of meat, etc. — but if he found it in another place we are concerned until he has simanim and recognizes it by teviyat ayin (meaning: or recognizes it); and likewise if he sent it via an idolater the law is thus, for we say in Perek Ein Ma'amidin (Avodah Zarah daf 39): barrels are forbidden with one seal, end of his words — for at first glance it is difficult why he wrote 'and likewise,' etc., and what did he innovate here. And according to what I wrote it is settled: for Rav it is not permitted here by teviyat ayin, and since it is settled like Levi — permitted by teviyat ayin. And if so, Mordechai wrote well here regarding sending a slaughtered chicken via an idolater: at first they wanted to seek permission because of the slaughterer if he would recognize it, and it did not succeed in their hands, and they permitted because of the chicken owner's recognition by teviyat ayin — and this is Levi, as I wrote above:

baer_heitev.he: שהניחו. כ' הט"ז אע"פ שלא נתן דעתו אם הוא במקום שהניחו או לא אין נוהגין לאסרו אפי' ברוב טבחים עובדי כוכבים והש"ך השיג עליו ומסיק דוקא באותו מקום עצמו הא לאו הכי אסור. ואם הניח עשר ומצא תשע מסקנת הש"ך דאם אינם קשורים מותר ואם הם קשורים אסור ועי' בא"ח סימן תל"ט בט"ז כ' בשם המרדכי מעשה בא לידי בתרנגולת שחוטה ושלחוה ביד עובד כוכבים בלי שומר ונסתפק לומר שמא אחרת היתה ושאלו להשוחט אם שחט זאת התרנגולת ואמר אין לי בה ט"ע אמנם עתה שחטתי תרנגולת א' ובעל התרנגולת היה מכיר אותה ואמר שזאת היא והתרתי כיון שהבעל מכירה כר"ת דאמר לית הלכתא כרב דאמר בשר שנתעלם אסור והקשה הב"י דהא רב נמי מכשיר בט"ע דעדיף מסי' והט"ז תירץ דס"ל להמרדכי דלרב לא מהני ט"ע אלא במקום שאין ריעותא כגון שנמצא בשר ביד עובד כוכבים שלקח לעצמו ורוב המוכרים ישראל למה לנו לומר שהחליפו והחמירו מכח חומרא שצריך ט"ע משא"כ אם ישראל שולח ע"י עובד כוכבים בשר או עוף שחוט שיש חשש שמא החליפו עובד כוכבים להנאתו שנתן גרוע ממנו בזה י"ל דלרב לא מהני ט"ע לכן כ' המרדכי דקי"ל כלוי ואף בנדון זה מהני ט"ע וק"ל:
baer_heitev.en: Where he left it. Taz wrote: even if he did not pay attention whether it is in the place where he left it or not — they are not accustomed to forbid it, even where most slaughterers are idolaters. And Shach challenged him and concluded: specifically in that very place itself; otherwise — forbidden. And if he left ten and found nine — Shach's conclusion: if they are not tied — permitted; if tied — forbidden. And see Orach Chaim siman 439; Taz wrote in the name of Mordechai: an incident came before me with a slaughtered chicken sent in the hand of an idolater without a guard, and they were in doubt to say perhaps it was another; and they asked the slaughterer if he slaughtered this chicken, and he said: I have no teviyat ayin upon it; however, I have just now slaughtered one chicken; and the chicken's owner recognized it and said this is it, and I permitted it, since the owner recognizes it like Rabbenu Tam, who said the halacha is not like Rav who said meat that disappeared from sight is forbidden. And Beit Yosef challenged: behold Rav too permits with teviyat ayin, which is preferable to siman; and Taz answered that Mordechai holds that for Rav teviyat ayin does not help except where there is no suspicious circumstance — such as when meat is found in the hand of an idolater who took for himself and most sellers are Israelites — why say it was exchanged; they were stringent from the force of stringency that teviyat ayin is required. Not so if an Israelite sends via an idolater slaughtered meat or bird where there is concern the idolater exchanged for his benefit, giving worse than it — here one may say that for Rav teviyat ayin does not help; therefore Mordechai wrote that it is settled like Levi, and even in this case teviyat ayin helps — requires further study:

beer_hagolah.he:
לשון הרמב"ם שם:
טור בשם יש מחלקין וכ"כ הרמב"ן והרשב"א:
שם בשם רשב"ם וה"ה בשם יש מן האחרונים ושכן כתב הרשב"א:
beer_hagolah.en:
The Rambam's wording there:
Tur in the name of 'there are those who distinguish,' and so Ramban and Rashba:
There in the name of Rashbam, and likewise in the name of some of the later authorities, and so Rashba wrote:

beur_hagra.he:
תלה כו' ואם תלאו כו'. מפרש ההיא דשילהי י"ט בנפלו החתיכות לארץ:
ויש מתירין כו'. שפ' דלא כרב דכל הני מתני' דמייתי שם תשע חנויות ומצא בה בשר ונמצא בגבולין דלא כרב ואע"ג דשנינהו שינויי דחיקי נינהו וקאמר שם ורב היכי אכיל כו' ול"ק היכא אכלינן בישרא ועובדא דרב כהנא שם דלא כרב וכן בפ"ב דב"מ עובדא דר"ה ועובדא דר' אמי וההיא דשלהי י"מ תלמידי דרב הוי וההיא דפ"ב דב"מ שנטלו העורב בההיא מודינן דע"כ לא קי"ל כרב אלא שמצאו במקום שהניחו [וז"ש אם מצאו כו' וע' סה"ת סי' מ"ז] והנהו עובדי דשם דא"ל אית לך סימנא בגווה כו' מיירי בעיר שרובה עובדי כוכבים וז"ש בהג"ה
ואפי' אם כו' וכמ"ש בנמצא ביד עובד כוכבים אע"ג דאליבא דרב הוא כ"ש לדידן וכ"ש בנמצא בשוק:
(ליקוט) וי"מ כו' במקום שהניחו. עתוס' דב"מ כ"ג ב' ד"ה מחרוזות כו' כ"ד ב' ד"ה אתא כו' וכ"כ בסה"ת ובת"ה וברא"ש וש"פ (ע"כ):
beur_hagra.en:
He hung, etc., and if he hung it, etc. He explains that which is at the end of chapter 19, when the pieces fell to the ground:
And there are those who permit, etc. He explains not like Rav, for all those mishnayot he brings there — nine shops, and found in the borders not like Rav — and even though we answered that these are forced answers, he says there: and Rav, how does he eat, etc. And there is no difficulty where do we eat among Israelites; and the incident of Rav Kahana there is not like Rav; and likewise in chapter 2 of Bava Metzia the incident of R' Huna and the incident of R' Ami; and that which is at the end of chapter 10, disciples of Rav — and that which is in chapter 2 of Bava Metzia where ravens took it — in that we agree that presumably we do not rule like Rav, but only when he found it in the place where he left it [and this is what is written 'if he found it,' etc.; and see Sefer HaTerumah siman 47]. And those incidents there where they said to him: do you have a siman inside it, etc. — deal with a city that is mostly idolaters — and this is what is written in the hagahah:
And even if, etc., and as written regarding found in the hand of an idolater — even though according to Rav it is all the more so for us; and all the more so regarding found in the market:
(Likkut) And some say, etc., in the place where he left it. From Tosafot Bava Metzia 23b s.v. mecharuzot, etc., 24b s.v. ata, etc.; and so in Sefer HaTerumah and Taharat HaKodesh and Rosh and Shitah Mekubetzet (end of his words):

pitchei_teshuva.he: והמנהג להקל. עיין מ"ש ט"ז בפירוש דברי המרדכי ועיין בתשובת כנסת יחזקאל סימן ל"ט. ועיין בשו"ת ארבעה טורי אבן סימן ז':
pitchei_teshuva.en: And the custom is to be lenient. See what Taz wrote explaining Mordechai's words; and see responsum Knesset Yechezkel siman 39; and see in responsa Arba'ah Turim Even siman 7:

nekudot_hakesef.he: (ט"ז ס"ק ב') מ"ש מחמץ בפסח כו'. זה אינו כמ"ש בש"ך ס"ק ח' דהכא נמי מיירי בקשורים כמו גבי חמץ:
nekudot_hakesef.en: (Taz s.k. 2) What he wrote from chametz on Pesach, etc. This is not as Shach wrote s.k. 8, that here too it deals with tied pieces like regarding chametz:

kaf_hachayim.he: ב) שם. וכבר אסרו חכמים כל הבשר וכו' והוא מגמ' חולין צ"ה ע"א אמר רב בשר כיון שנתעלם מן העין אסור ופירש"י אסור שמא נתחלף בנבלה. והגם שיש חולקין כתב ב"י לענין הלכה כיון שהרי"פ והרמב"ם מסכימים לפסוק כרב יש לאסור בשר שנתעלם מן העין ואין לו בו סימן ולא טביעות עין אלא א"כ תלאו במסמר וכיוצא בו שא"א לשרץ ליטול ולהניח עכ"ל וע"כ פסק כן בש"ע.
kaf_hachayim.en: (2) There. And the Sages already forbade all meat, etc. And it is from the Gemara Chullin 95a: Rav said — meat, once it disappeared from sight, is forbidden; and Rashi explained: forbidden lest it was exchanged for nevelah. And although there are disputants, Beit Yosef wrote regarding practical halacha: since Rif and Rambam agree to rule like Rav, one must forbid meat that disappeared from sight that has neither siman nor teviyat ayin, unless he hung it on a nail and the like such that it is impossible for a creeping thing to take and replace, end of his words; and therefore he ruled thus in Shulchan Aruch.

kereti.he:
ויש מתירין כו' היינו אם הניחה במקום שמצאה מבלי שינוי כשר אפילו רוב טבחי גוים דאמרינן היא היא החתיכה שלקח אבל אם לא מצאוה במקום שהניחה דיש ריעותא חיישינן לעורב דהחליפו היינו לא ממקום רחוק רק ממקום קרוב מאותו עיר ואם בעיר רוב טבחי ישראל מותר ואם לאו אסור אם לא בסימן וט"ע כהנ"ל כן משמע מדברי בעה"ת עיין ש"ך סק"ח:
במקום שהניחה ואם הניח יו"ד ומצא ט' דעת הש"ך ואחרונים דאם הם בלתי מקושרין ודאי לא חיישינן אבל אם הם מקושרים (וצ"ל קשר הרגיל דאל"ה הוי קשר סימן) והניח תשע ומצא ח' יש לחוש להחמיר בעיר שרובו טבחי נכרים:
שהניחה וכו' ואם מסופק אם הוא במקום שהניח אסור ש"ך
שכל המוכרים ה"ה רובו ככולו:
בשר כשר אבל אם לפעמים מוכרין טריפה אסור דה"ל כמקום שאין מכריזין דאסור ליקח:
kereti.en:
And there are those who permit, etc. — this is if he left it in the place where he found it without change — permitted even if most slaughterers are gentiles, for we say: it is the same piece he took; but if he did not find it in the place where he left it — there is suspicious circumstance, we are concerned for a raven that exchanged it — not from a far place, only from a place near that city; and if in the city most slaughterers are Israelites — permitted; if not — forbidden unless with siman and teviyat ayin as above — so is implied from Beit Yosef's words; see Shach s.k. 8:
In the place where he left it; and if he left ten and found nine — Shach's and later authorities' view: if they are not tied — certainly we are not concerned; but if tied (and it should say: the usual tie, for otherwise it is a tie-siman) and he left nine and found eight — there is reason to be stringent in a city where most slaughterers are gentiles:
Where he left it, etc.; and if he is in doubt whether it is in the place where he left it — forbidden — Shach:
That all the sellers — the majority is like the whole:
Kosher meat; but if they sometimes sell treifah — forbidden, for it is like a place where they do not announce, that it is forbidden to buy:
